redFlags: Chest pain, focal neurological deficit, severe breathlessness or syncope discovered during screening
Markedly elevated blood pressure with acute target-organ symptoms
Suicidal ideation or immediate safeguarding concern
Alarm cancer symptoms such as unexplained bleeding, persistent mass or major unintentional weight loss
symptoms: Often asymptomatic attendance for preventive review
May disclose fatigue, low mood, sleep problems or reduced function during structured history
May report tobacco exposure, inactivity, unhealthy diet or occupational risk
May have overdue vaccination or cancer screening
physicalSigns: Raised body-mass index or waist circumference
Oral-health, vision, hearing or mobility concerns
Abnormal findings requiring conversion from screening to a diagnostic pathway

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Asymptomatic, eligible by age or risk and suitable for a validated screening intervention.
Known diagnosis or repeated abnormal result requiring disease-specific targets rather than screening thresholds.
Symptoms or signs raise pre-test probability and require diagnostic, not screening, tests.
Single clinic value is not confirmed on repeat or out-of-office measurement.

ruleIn.testName: Standardised blood-pressure measurement with out-of-office confirmation
ruleIn.modalityTarget: Standardised blood-pressure measurement with out-of-office confirmation — Hypertension
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Persistently elevated readings confirmed outside the clinic when indicated.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Reduces misclassification from technique, white-coat effect and isolated readings.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Risk-based glucose testing — Prediabetes or diabetes
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Abnormal fasting glucose, random glucose in context or glycated haemoglobin confirmed through the diagnostic pathway.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: PHA guidance begins routine adult testing at the defined age and earlier with overweight plus risk factors.

ruleIn.testName: Age-, sex- and risk-appropriate cancer screening
ruleIn.modalityTarget: Age-, sex- and risk-appropriate cancer screening — Preclinical breast, colorectal, cervical or lung cancer
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Negative screening at the recommended interval or an abnormal result requiring timely diagnostic confirmation.
ruleIn.targetCondition: Preclinical breast, colorectal, cervical or lung cancer
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Benefit depends on eligibility, interval and complete follow-through after an abnormal screen.

ruleOut.testName: Repeat or confirmatory diagnostic test after an abnormal screen
ruleOut.modalityTarget: Repeat or confirmatory diagnostic test after an abnormal screen — False-positive screening result
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Diagnostic testing does not confirm disease.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Screening tests do not by themselves establish many diagnoses.

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Medication and comorbidity review — Secondary or iatrogenic risk
ruleOut.expectedFinding: A medicine, pregnancy state, renal disease or other condition explains or changes the preventive finding.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Prevents inappropriate application of general-population screening or treatment advice.

pathophysiology.summary: Periodic health examination is a risk-based preventive-care process rather than a disease episode. It identifies modifiable cardiovascular, metabolic, cancer, infectious, mental-health and functional risks before symptoms or irreversible complications develop, while avoiding screening that has an unfavourable balance of benefit and harm.
keyMechanisms: Age, sex, family history, exposures and comorbidity alter baseline disease probability and screening benefit.
Repeated measurement can detect trajectories in blood pressure, adiposity, glycaemia and lipids before complications emerge.
Evidence-based screening shifts selected cancers and chronic diseases toward earlier diagnosis.
Shared decisions reduce harms from false positives, overdiagnosis and preventive medicines with small net benefit.

clinicalManagement.title: Build an individual risk inventory
actions: Record age, sex, pregnancy potential, family history, tobacco exposure, occupation, medicines, comorbidity and prior screening.
Assess mental health, safety, function and social determinants with validated tools where appropriate.
Separate asymptomatic screening from symptoms that require diagnostic evaluation.

clinicalManagement.title: Complete core measurements
actions: Measure blood pressure using validated technique and assess body-mass index and waist circumference at the PHA interval.
Order glucose and lipid testing according to age and risk.
Review oral health, vaccination status and age-related vision, hearing, falls or cognition needs.

clinicalManagement.title: Offer eligible screening
actions: Offer breast, cervical, colorectal, lung, osteoporosis and abdominal-aortic-aneurysm screening only when age, sex and risk criteria are met.
Explain likely benefits, limitations and follow-up before testing.
Create a closed-loop plan for every abnormal result.

clinicalManagement.title: Deliver preventive interventions
actions: Provide indicated immunisation under the current Saudi schedule.
Offer tobacco-cessation treatment, physical-activity and dietary support.
Use generic preventive pharmacotherapy only after formal cardiovascular-risk, contraindication and shared-decision assessment.
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At the same visit or scheduled follow-up

clinicalManagement.title: Close the preventive-care loop
actions: Communicate normal and abnormal results in understandable language.
Convert confirmed abnormalities to the relevant diagnostic or chronic-care pathway.
Update the recall date and assign ownership for referrals and pending tests.

nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Maintain a personalised recall schedule based on the 2023 PHA age and risk tables, review abnormal results promptly, and update eligibility whenever health status, family history, pregnancy status or exposure changes.
mdtReferrals: Primary-care nurse or preventive-care coordinator for recall and result tracking
Dietitian, tobacco-cessation service or exercise professional according to risk
Mental-health service for confirmed depression, anxiety or safety concern
Diagnostic specialty pathway for any abnormal screening result
lifestyleAndDiet: Support a sustainable dietary pattern rich in vegetables, fruit, whole grains and minimally processed foods while accounting for culture and comorbidity.
Encourage regular aerobic and strengthening activity adapted to ability.
Provide tobacco cessation, sleep, weight and oral-health support without stigma.
patientEducation: Explain that preventive tests are selected by personal risk and that more testing is not always safer.
Use shared decision making for preference-sensitive cancer screening and preventive medicines.
Give accessible instructions for preparation, result access and the next step after an abnormal result.
dischargeCriteria: Risk profile, due interventions and deferred shared decisions are documented.
Every test and referral has a named owner and result-communication method.
Urgent symptoms or severe abnormalities have been diverted to immediate assessment.
